definition: Convulsive disorder is a diagnostic term for a condition involving convulsions or seizures. In this source, it appears as a prior seizure-related history that may increase the likelihood of later seizures.

reasons: The packet does not describe “convulsive disorder” as a diagnostic term or define it as such; it only refers to “history of convulsive disorder” as a covariate/risk factor.

The claim that this history “may increase the likelihood of later seizures” is only supported in the packet’s statement that patients with “a history of convulsive disorder … [are] more likely to have seizures,” but the definition’s wording (“diagnostic term” and “later seizures”) goes beyond what is explicitly stated.

The packet only shows “history of convulsive disorder” as a covariate and notes that such history has been reported to be associated with later seizures; it does not support defining the term itself as a diagnostic term for a condition involving convulsions or seizures.
The wording generalizes beyond the source by treating this as a settled diagnostic definition rather than a usage in one study’s background section.
